tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: The British Indian Ocean Territory is an United Kingdom overseas territory in the Indian Ocean. As such, it is counted as **the UK** for country streaks purposes. Beware that none of the coverage is considered pinpointable, and as a result you are unlikely to get it in most community-made maps. As such, this guide is mainly intended to give a general idea of what type of coverage you can find on the islands.

tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: Coverage was taken with a Generation 3 **trekker**.

tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: Coverage is mostly found on small atolls in the northern half of the territory.

tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: A large portion of the coverage is taken on sand beaches. You will typically see many palm trees along the beaches.

tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: Coastal palm forests also comprise a significant portion of the coverage. They almost exclusively consist of coconut palms.

tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: Mangroves can be found on several of the atolls.

tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: Some of the larger islands with coverage have grassy fields surrounded by bushes and palms.

tips.section: Identifying the British Indian Ocean Territory
tips.text: The trekker can occasionally be found walking offshore in the water.

spotlights.text: Coin du Mire is a small island with a dark **rocky shore** and a grassy field with **no bushes or palm trees**.
A white medium-sized **shipwreck** can be found on the beach at the eastern tip of Nelsons Island.
